title: Agentic AI for Gravitational Wave Data Analysis: A Head-to-Head Comparison of Coding Agents Executing a Matched Filter Pipeline on Einstein Telescope Simulated Data
abstract: arXiv:2605.28916v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We report a methodological study of agentic AI in gravitational-wave data analysis: two systems, Claude Code (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI), autonomously executed the same simple end-to-end pipeline on Einstein Telescope (ET) simulated data, on shared infrastructure and without human intervention. The object of study is the behaviour, reliability and auditability of the agents, not the physics output, used here as a controlled test case. The pipeline comprises power spectral density estimation from simulated ET noise, geometric template bank generation with IMRPhenomD waveforms, matched-filter recovery of 100 binary black hole injections, results generation, and LLM-assisted production of a LaTeX manuscript in Physical Review D style. Both agents received identical specifications and resources. The experiment was run twice: first with unrealistically loud injections, then with signals rescaled to a physically motivated SNR rang

translated_title: 用于引力波数据分析的智能体AI：编程智能体在爱因斯坦望远镜模拟数据上执行匹配滤波管线的正面对比
translated_abstract: 我们报告了一项关于智能体AI在引力波数据分析中的方法学研究：两个系统——Claude Code（Anthropic）和Codex（OpenAI）——在共享基础设施上、无人工干预的情况下，自主地在爱因斯坦望远镜（ET）模拟数据上执行了相同的简单端到端管线。研究对象是智能体的行为、可靠性和可审计性，而非物理输出，后者在此仅作为受控测试用例。该管线包括：从模拟ET噪声中进行功率谱密度估计、使用IMRPhenomD波形生成几何模板库、对100个双黑洞注入信号进行匹配滤波恢复、结果生成，以及借助大语言模型辅助产出符合《Physical Review D》格式的LaTeX手稿。两个智能体获得了完全相同的规范和资源。实验运行了两次：第一次使用不切实际的过强信号注入，第二次将信号重新缩放到具有物理合理性的信噪比范围内……
tldr: 该研究让Anthropic的Claude Code与OpenAI的Codex两个编程智能体在完全相同条件下无人工干预地自主完成爱因斯坦望远镜模拟引力波数据的匹配滤波分析全流程，系统对比了智能体AI在科学计算中的行为、可靠性与可审计性。
en_tdlr: This study has two coding agents—Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex—autonomously execute an identical matched-filter pipeline on Einstein Telescope simulated gravitational-wave data under identical conditions, providing a systematic head-to-head comparison of agentic AI behavior, reliability, and auditability in scientific computing.
